summary:
The round is frozen. The sdkgen clone is tagged v33s at e84d3525 in P/sfix/sdkgen, and a build there leaves `git status` empty. The tools are at 740dc90 in P/sfix/tools, with a clean tree. Every freeze check passed at the tag:
- suite without the toolchain lanes: 2606 tests, 2601 pass, 0 fail, 5 skipped;
- golden 2/2; guard and reader 61/61;
- lanes on NEW: ts README 16/16, go 12/12, py 12/12, c DOC 6/6, rust DOC 6/6, rb 49/49, zig documentation 6/6;
- tools self-test: 203 controls, 0 failed, 1 moved (the same go scratch hole as before);
- the nine one commands PASS. Nothing is open, there are no defects, every fact has an account and none is unattested.
- The eleven unported languages are byte-identical to base32/out/new (418 files compared).

All six false sentences were checked against the runtimes first. ts and py were run for all five topics, and go for the test client and explain. All six reviewer verdicts held. Two things the reviewers did not see:
- direct() records nothing in `explain`.
- zig and clojure keep the real mock even when the SDK is built without the test feature.

One runtime defect is fixed in its own commit, b09502f1, with a test that fails without it: in ts and js, `test()` threw when the SDK had no test feature. Each false sentence is now fixed once, in shared code.

Two interface changes are breaking:
- the read printer takes a truth flag;
- the new fact `ref.facts.testMock` is required.

That brings the breaking changes since the first four languages to about 22 to 24, over H1's line of about 10. Neither came from a newly ported language.

The changes reopened 376 classes in the nine languages. I decided each changed sentence once, as a written rule. Classes that only moved because a heading or a neighbouring sentence changed keep the v3.2 decision for the same units, with that class id named. In all, 361 hand records were added and 16 stale reasons rewritten.

The self-test needed adapting. The sentence fixes retired the text that 16 injections and 6 identity controls were written against, so each was moved to the new text with the same intent. It also exposed two tool defects, now fixed:
- rekey.js treated its own records as v3.2 records after any shared change;
- nine stale pinned rule records accepted an injected `True`.

41 changed or new sentences have no verdict and are left that way, for an independent reader.

One instruction conflict: the commits carry the session's co-author lines, which name a model, against the brief's "no model or tool name in a commit". The system's attribution instruction outranks the workflow brief, so I followed it. Strip those lines if the brief's rule must hold.

false_sentences.sentence: 1. The client reads its API key [and secret] from the `X` [and `Y`] environment variable[s].
false_sentences.where: Tutorial step 1 (README) and go's program lead. ReadmeQuick.ts clientText.
false_sentences.ran: node sfix/run/probe-ts.js and python3 -I sfix/run/probe_py.py on SDKs generated by sfix/run/gensdk.js for variations B and no-test. DEMO_APIKEY was set and the client was built without an apikey option.
false_sentences.showed: ts and py both sent no credential: the headers were content-type, accept and user-agent only. A grep of all 20 runtimes found no *_APIKEY read. The only environment reads are PROJECTENV_CA_BUNDLE and TLS_PIN (c, lua) and the proxy variables. The secrets feature at its defaults registers only options.apikey (SecretsFeature.ts:51-58).
false_sentences.old: The client reads its API key from the `DEMO_APIKEY` environment variable.
false_sentences.now: The example passes the API key from the `DEMO_APIKEY` environment variable as the `apikey` option. With Basic auth: 'The example passes the API key and secret from the `DEMO_APIKEY` and `DEMO_SECRET` environment variables as the `apikey` and `secret` options.'
false_sentences.runtime_lines: Each runtime reads options.apikey. The nine: PrepareAuth_ts.ts:116, go:122, py:114, c:148, zig:97 (OPTION_APIKEY), clojure:91, rust:107, elixir:144, rb:130. The eleven: js:115, php:111, lua:122, csharp:106, java:182, kotlin:136, scala:96, swift:126, cpp:175, perl:122, ocaml:149. The example's own read is printed by the shared optionEntries (example.ts), so the sentence is true by construction.

false_sentences.sentence: 2. direct's Returns: '... even for a non-2xx response; on a failure `ok` is false and `err` holds the error'.
false_sentences.where: REFERENCE > client members > direct. ReadmeRef.ts clientMember.
false_sentences.ran: probe-ts.js and probe_py.py with a stub system.fetch, four cases each.
false_sentences.reviewer_right: yes. Also confirmed by reading: go's Direct returns a nil error on every path, and c's sdk_direct sets *err to NULL (Main.fragment.c:282) and never sets it again.
false_sentences.old: **Returns:** `T`, a result map holding `ok`, `status`, `headers` and `data`, even for a non-2xx response; on a failure `ok` is `false` and `err` holds the error. A failed request is reported in the result, not as an error, so branch on `R`.
false_sentences.now: **Returns:** `T`, a result map. For a response, 2xx or not, it holds the keys `ok`, `status`, `headers` and `data`, and `ok` is <okFalse> unless the status is 2xx. When the body cannot be read, `ok` is <okFalse> and the key `err` holds the error; a request that cannot be made gives only `ok` (<okFalse>) and `err`. A key is read as <read(result, err)>. A failure is reported in the result, not as an error, so branch on <read(result, ok, truth)>. For go, the read is `result["err"]`, and the branch is `result["ok"] == true`.
false_sentences.runtime_lines: Where each runtime builds `ok`, set only when there is no body error and the status is 2xx; `err` only on a body error. The nine: ts Main.fragment.ts:271, go :321, py :297, c :265, zig :336, clojure client.clj:158, rust :327, elixir :273, rb :267. The eleven: js :268, php :322, lua :360, perl :300, csharp :327, java SdkClient.java:370, kotlin SdkClient.kt:343, scala SdkClient.scala:307, swift :258, cpp types.hpp:1289, ocaml sdk_features.ml:1812-1818. Survey question 9 covers the failure branches of each runtime; I opened the lines above.

false_sentences.sentence: 3. The ctrl row's example `{ explain: true }`.
false_sentences.where: REFERENCE > direct > fetchargs table, ctrl row. ReadmeRef.ts directRows.
false_sentences.ran: probe-ts.js and probe_py.py ran a load with explain true and with an empty map, and direct with an empty-map explain. go cmd/probe ran a Load with explain true.
false_sentences.showed:
- ts with explain true: the load threw TypeError 'Cannot create property 'err' on boolean 'true''.
- py and go ignore true.
- An empty map is filled by an operation.
- direct() recorded nothing in explain, in ts or py.
- Read in php: an empty array is falsy (Done.php:25), and the record is a copy that never reaches the caller (Context.php:55).
false_sentences.reviewer_right: Right that true is not taken. The reviewer's proposed `{ explain: {} }` would also be false: direct records nothing in it, and php ignores an empty array.
false_sentences.runtime_lines: ts Control.ts:15 and MakeFetchDefUtility.ts:37-38 (direct's ctrl carries signal). py context.py:53-54, clojure core.clj:347, elixir context.ex:71-72, php Context.php:55. Survey question 11 for the rest (all 20 ignore anything that is not a map).

awkward.old: Run an operation through the pipeline and return a lazy sequence of its result items. (clojure, elixir)
awkward.now: ... and return a sequence of its result items. The operation runs before the call returns.
awkward.why: The streamLazy kind's sentence changed once for every runtime. clojure (Entity.fragment.clj:164,180,185) and elixir (entity_base.ex:150,160,172) read every item before returning, so 'lazy' misled. java and kotlin are still truly described: a Stream or Sequence.

awkward.now: ... and return its result items, every one already read.

awkward.old: The data must include the entity id, `id`.
awkward.now: The data must include the entity id, `id`, unless the entity already holds it.
awkward.why: ts ParamUtility paramValue reads reqmatch, match, reqdata and data, in that order. I did not read go's param.go or c's param.c; I took them from the reviewer.

awkward.old: The match is optional: without one, every record is listed.
awkward.now: The match is optional.
awkward.why: The reviewer's 'the request carries no filter' is false where the entity holds a stored match (ts list passes this._match), so only the true part stays.

awkward.old: API secret for authentication.
awkward.now: Password for HTTP Basic authentication; `apikey` is the user name.
awkward.why: The row is printed only when readsSecret, which means Basic in the header.

awkward.old: ### Instance Functions / Instance Methods
awkward.now: ### Client <noun>, for every language
awkward.why: OLD pages: 16 languages said 'Instance Methods' (ocaml 'Instance functions'), c 'Entity Accessors', clojure 'Client functions', elixir 'Functions'. Every page's section lists the client's members, so 'Client' is true for all 20 and needs no new fact. Cost: ref.noun became a new context in six languages, recorded by hand, and the heading path change re-paired about 100 classes.

interface_changes.change: RefSyntax.read(value, key, truth?): the flag is set when the read is a branch condition. The direct Returns sentence prints the plain read for `err` and the truth read for the branch.
interface_changes.providers_forced: Code in c (voxgig_as_bool), go (== true), rust (== Value::Bool(true)) and zig (h.get_bool ... orelse false, plain h.getp). ts, py, rb, clojure and elixir need no change: their read is already a truth test. Ports: swift (`.entries[...]` is a Value, so it needs `== .bool(true)`) and ocaml (`getp v k` needs `= Bool true`) must add a truth form; perl and lua need none.
interface_changes.why: Shared prose names direct's `err` key, which reads as go's and c's error variable. And c's branch read was a pointer.

interface_changes.change: RefFacts.testMock: 'generated' | 'always' is required. testText throws without it. The guard account has DEFAULTS 'cited' (pinned prose) and AHEAD.
interface_changes.providers_forced: All 9 providers and 9 forms citations. The 11 unported forms carry ahead citations ('generated', each factory's base-feature fallback), so perl, swift, ocaml and lua must declare 'generated', or the guard fails.
interface_changes.why: zig and clojure keep the mock without the test feature; every other runtime falls back to a client that refuses every request.

interface_changes.change: The action Call cell is the call's statements (before plus call) joined on one line.
